name: Top-k singular values via power iteration
task: Create /tmp/eval_svd/svd.py with top_singular_values(matrix, k) returning a list of the k largest singular values of `matrix` (descending). Use power iteration on A^T A with deflation: iterate v ← (A^T A) v, normalize, orthogonalize against previously found right singular vectors. Square root the eigenvalue to recover σ.

validation.script:
import importlib.util; spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('m','/tmp/eval_svd/svd.py'); mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(mod); T = mod.top_singular_values; s = T([[5,0],[0,3]], 2); assert abs(s[0] - 5) < 1e-6 and abs(s[1] - 3) < 1e-6; s2 = T([[3,0],[0,4],[0,0]], 2); assert abs(s2[0] - 4) < 1e-6 and abs(s2[1] - 3) < 1e-6
import math; g = (1 + math.sqrt(5)) / 2; s3 = T([[1,1],[0,1]], 2); assert len(s3) == 2 and abs(s3[0] - g) < 1e-6 and abs(s3[1] - 1/g) < 1e-6, f'[[1,1],[0,1]] has singular values {g}, {1/g}: got {s3}'
s4 = T([[2,0,1],[1,3,0],[0,1,4],[1,1,1]], 2); assert len(s4) == 2 and abs(s4[0] - 4.6807229) < 1e-5 and abs(s4[1] - 3.0514903) < 1e-5, f'[[2,0,1],[1,3,0],[0,1,4],[1,1,1]] has top singular values 4.6807229, 3.0514903: got {s4}'
print('OK')
